articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and the hilariously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently nobody can write secure code anymore.

articles.title: Radar Trends to Watch: May 2026
articles.summary: Palo Alto's PAN-OS gets pwned by a critical buffer overflow (CVE-2026-0300) that's being actively exploited in the wild. Nothing says 'enterprise security' like a 9.3 CVSS score and unauthenticated RCE.

articles.title: Real estate giant confirms vishing incident as ShinyHunters and Qilin both come knocking
articles.summary: Fresh Linux 'CopyFail' vulnerability drops with a reliable root exploit, and surprise—attackers didn't waste time putting it to work. Researchers basically handed out root shells like candy.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turns old routers into token-stealing goldmines, mass harvesting Microsoft Office authentication tokens. Your ancient Linksys is now Moscow's favorite backdoor.

articles.title: Your work apps are quietly handing 19 data points to someone
articles.summary: A 15-year-old just casually breached France Titres and put 12-18 million government records up for sale on the dark web. French cybersecurity: apparently no match for a teenager with free time.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: EFF calls for dismantling the 'turnkey totalitarian state' that NSA whistleblower William Binney warned about. Politicians change, but the surveillance empire remains—time to take back our digital rights.

articles.title: India orders infosec red alert in case Mythos sparks crime spree
articles.summary: UK's age-gating plans could break the entire internet, privacy groups warn. Instead of targeting Big Tech's surveillance capitalism, ministers want to ID-gate everything—classic misdirection.

articles.title: Windows Phone Link Exploited by CloudZ RAT to Steal Credentials and OTPs
articles.summary: Google launches Binary Transparency for Android to fight supply chain attacks by creating a public ledger of legitimate apps. Finally, some actual innovation in mobile security that isn't just more surveillance.

articles.title: Middle East Cyber Battle Field Broadens — Especially in UAE
articles.summary: Dark Reading celebrates 20 years by cataloging the biggest cyber events from Stuxnet to ChatGPT. Two decades of digital chaos, from industrial sabotage to AI hallucinations—what a ride.

articles.title: 15-year-old detained over massive data breach at French government agency
articles.summary: 2026 becomes the year AI-powered attacks go mainstream, starting with a 17-year-old using automated tools to breach 7 million records from Japan's largest internet cafe chain. The script kiddies have AI now.
